government.note: Wikipedia describes the state as a unitary theocratic elective absolute monarchy. The sovereign entity is the Holy See; the Pope, elected for life by a conclave of cardinals, holds full legislative, executive and judicial power. He delegates legislation to the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State (appointed members; laws go to the Pope through the Secretariat of State before taking effect) and day-to-day administration to the President of the Governorate, who also presides over the Commission. Modelled as 'absolute_monarchy' because no elective-monarchy type exists; succession is by conclave, not heredity. There are no political parties and no popular elections.

offices.note: The President of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State also serves as President of the Governorate, the de facto head of government (the Pope delegates day-to-day executive power). Under the conclave rules the President's term formally ends when the papacy falls vacant; the Wikipedia list shows Szoka's and Vérgez Alzaga's tenures continuing across the 2005 and 2025 vacancies, and this timeline follows the list.

offices.note: Heads the Secretariat of State of the Holy See, which conducts its diplomacy and coordinates the Roman Curia. An office of the Holy See rather than of the Vatican City State, recorded because it is the most senior governing post after the Pope; laws of the Pontifical Commission reach the Pope through it.

no_parties_reason: Vatican City is an elective absolute monarchy under the Pope with no political parties and no popular elections. Legislation is prepared by the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State, whose members are cardinals and officials appointed by the Pope; it is not recorded as a legislature because no fetched source gives its composition on 1 January 2000.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Gameplay estimate, not measured data: there are no parties or elections, and the small resident population consists mainly of clergy, religious and Swiss Guards. christian_conservative is the closest existing id to the Holy See's Catholic religious governance; it is not a judgement of any individual's views.
